glossary.definition: The core scheduler abstraction: a pure transition that consumes the user's grade on a review and the elapsed time since the last review and returns, per candidate button, a next memory state and a next interval. Both algorithm families conform; fsrs-rs's API is literally next_states(previous_memory_state, desired_retention, elapsed_days) [FACT - fsrs-rs README quickstart].

Two mandatory scheduler inputs: response-dependence = the interval depends on the grade; time-dependence = it depends on actual elapsed time. SM-2 is response-dependent but time-blind (assumes on-time review); classic Anki patched time ad hoc (days_late credit); FSRS is natively both via R(t,S) [FACT - FAQ + The-Algorithm wiki].

FSRS's three-component memory state: Difficulty D in [1,10] (how hard it is to raise S), Stability S (days for retrievability to fall from 100% to 90%, i.e. the interval at which R=0.9), and Retrievability R (probability of recall now, the only component that decays without a review). Each card carries its own (D,S); R is computed from S and elapsed time [FACT - FSRS FAQ + algorithm wiki].

FSRS-6's trainable recall-decay law R(t,S)=(1+factor*t/S)^(-w20) with factor=0.9^(-1/w20)-1 chosen so R(S,S)=0.9; earlier versions fixed DECAY=-0.5, FACTOR=19/81 (v4.5/5) or DECAY=-1, FACTOR=1/9 (v4) [FACT - official algorithm wiki].

The single tuning knob r: the interval is the inverse curve at r, I(r,S)=(S/factor)(r^(-1/w20)-1), with I(0.9,S)=S by construction; Anki defaults r=0.90, and above ~0.90 workload rises steeply, above ~0.97 it can be overwhelming [FACT - The-Algorithm wiki + deck-options.md].

Workload vs retention is not monotone: raising r shortens intervals (more reviews) while lowering r causes more forgetting (more relearning), so a workload-minimizing retention exists. Anki's CMRR ('Compute minimum recommended retention') searches for it; going below it is dominated (more time AND less knowledge, knowledge approximated by the sum of R across cards) [FACT - The-Optimal-Retention wiki + deck-options.md].

Anki's review-log table, one row per review ever: (id epoch-ms, cid, usn, ease button 1-4, ivl, lastIvl, factor, time ms capped 60000, type 0=learn/1=review/2=relearn/3=cram). This exact shape is what the FSRS optimizer consumes and what AnkiConnect's insertReviews writes [FACT - AnkiDroid DB wiki + AnkiConnect README].

Fitting the FSRS w0..w20 vector to one user's own revlog: reviews grouped per card into (rating, interval) time-series, model trained by maximum-likelihood / binary log-loss on recall-vs-forget outcomes via backprop-through-time. In Anki it is the per-preset 'Optimize' button; monthly reoptimization suffices [FACT - mechanism-of-optimization wiki + deck-options.md].

Randomized jitter added on answering so cards introduced together and graded the same do not clump; Anki uses 1 day + 15% (2.5-7d) / 10% (7-20d) / 5% (>20d) banded ranges (learning cards up to 5 min), and it cannot be disabled [FACT - studying.md + fuzz.rs FUZZ_RANGES].

.colpkg = Anki Collection Package (whole collection, all decks, scheduling included; import replaces the collection); .apkg = Anki Deck Package (one deck + media, 'Include Scheduling Information' optional). Both are a zipped SQLite database (.anki2) plus media [FACT - exporting.md + AnkiDroid DB wiki].

Add-on 2055492159 exposing a local JSON HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8765 (request {action, version:6, params}, response {result, error}); relevant actions include addNotes, answerCards, getReviewsOfCards and insertReviews (direct revlog 9-tuple writes). Requires a running Anki, which is NOT installed in this build env, so live behavior is UNKNOWN this session [FACT for the documented surface - README mirror; UNKNOWN for live confirmation].

Offline Python library that writes an .apkg without Anki: Model (fields + qfmt/afmt + css), Note(model, fields), Deck(deck_id, name), Package(deck).write_to_file(); model_id/deck_id are hardcoded random 30-31-bit ints and Note.guid must be kept stable so re-imports update instead of duplicate [FACT - genanki README, PyPI 0.13.1 MIT].

nodes.definition: Establish the abstraction the whole KB is built on: a scheduler is exactly a pure function (grade, elapsed) -> next memory state + next interval, evaluated once per candidate answer button. Both algorithm families conform — SM-2's state is (EF, repetition n, last interval) transitioned on the grade q; FSRS's state is (D, S) transitioned on the grade and elapsed days, with fsrs-rs exposing it literally as next_states(previous_memory_state, desired_retention, elapsed_days) returning one candidate state+interval per button [FACT - fsrs-rs README quickstart]. Treating the scheduler as this contract (not a pile of if-statements) is what makes it swappable, testable and revlog-loggable. The contract's two inputs — response (grade) and time (elapsed) — are both mandatory; a scheduler that drops either is defective.

nodes.definition: Make elapsed time a first-class scheduler input. SM-2's structural blind spot is that it ignores the ACTUAL time between reviews — it assumes reviews happen on schedule and computes the next interval from EF and repetition count alone [FACT - SM-2 mirror; FAQ]. Classic Anki patched this ad hoc: answering later than scheduled earns credit, with Good using (current_interval + days_late/2) * ease_factor and Easy (current_interval + days_late) * ease_factor * easy_multiplier [FACT - review.rs lines 241-248]. FSRS handles it natively: retrievability R(t,S) is a function of elapsed t, and for an overdue-but-recalled card the stability gain converges to an upper bound rather than growing linearly as in SM-2/Anki [FACT - The-Algorithm wiki]. A homegrown scheduler must therefore capture elapsed_days per review, not just the grade.

nodes.definition: Model the SM-2 baseline (Wozniak, SuperMemo, 1987) as the reference the whole field descends from. Each item carries an E-Factor EF initialized 2.5; intervals are I(1)=1 day, I(2)=6 days, I(n)=I(n-1)*EF for n>2 (fractional intervals round up). After each repetition the grade q on 0-5 updates EF via EF' = EF + (0.1 - (5-q)(0.08 + (5-q)0.02)), floored at 1.3 (deltas: q5 +0.10, q4 0.00, q3 -0.14, q2 -0.32, q1 -0.54, q0 -0.80) [FACT by definition]. If q<3 the interval ladder restarts at I(1) WITHOUT changing EF (the EF update still ran). Key invariants: EF is per-item, growth is geometric in EF, the 1.3 floor caps minimum growth. nodes.definition: Model classic Anki's SM-2 variant as a set of concrete deviations, all FACT from the fetched Anki source/FAQ. (1) User-configurable learning steps (default 1m 10m) replace SM-2's fixed 1d/6d and a card 'graduates' after the last step; failures DURING learning do not touch ease ('the initial acquisition process does not influence a card's ease'). (2) Four answer buttons, one fail grade. (3) Ease deltas as constants: Again -0.20, Hard -0.15, Good 0, Easy +0.15 (EASE_FACTOR_*_DELTA in review.rs). (4) Ease floor 1.3 (MINIMUM_EASE_FACTOR), initial 2.5 (INITIAL_EASE_FACTOR). (5) Lapse: Again on a review card enters relearning and multiplies the interval by New Interval (default 0.00 = full reset; 0.20 keeps 20%); repeated lapses can flag a leech. (6) Late answers get credit (days_late). (7) Extra multipliers: Hard x1.2, Easy Bonus x1.30, Interval Modifier x1.00 default, Maximum Interval cap; new intervals (except Again) >= previous + 1 day. The interval-modifier<->retention identity: new modifier = log(desired%)/log(current%), and raising 85%->90% gives ~0.65 modifier (~35% more study for +5 pts).

nodes.definition: Model FSRS's DSR memory state, the second algorithm Anki ships (since 23.10) and the one this scheduler should prefer for maturity. Three components [FACT - FSRS FAQ + algorithm wiki]: Retrievability R = probability of recall now, decaying with time since last review and the ONLY component that changes without a review; Stability S = the number of days for R to fall from 100% to 90% (equivalently the interval at which R=0.9); Difficulty D in [1,10] = how hard it is to increase S by reviewing. Grades G are 1=again, 2=hard, 3=good, 4=easy; each card carries its own (D,S) and R is computed from S and elapsed time. FSRS descends from MaiMemo's DHP model, itself a variant of Wozniak's three-component DSR model. Anki's Rust core depends on the fsrs crate; py-fsrs (v6.3.1, MIT) and fsrs-rs (BSD-3) are the reusable implementations.

nodes.definition: Give the recall-decay law that turns (S, elapsed t) into a retrievability. FSRS-6 uses a power forgetting curve with a TRAINABLE decay: R(t,S) = (1 + factor * t/S)^(-w20), where factor = 0.9^(-1/w20) - 1 is chosen so that R(S,S) = 0.9 exactly — i.e. Stability is the interval at which retrievability equals 90% by construction [FACT - official algorithm wiki]. Earlier versions fixed the decay: FSRS-4.5/5 used DECAY=-0.5 and FACTOR=19/81; FSRS v4 used DECAY=-1 and FACTOR=1/9. The curve is the single most load-bearing FSRS equation: it defines what S means, feeds the spacing effect (recall gains more when R is low), and is the function the next-interval computation inverts.

nodes.definition: Compute the next interval by INVERTING the forgetting curve at the desired retention r. Setting R(t,S)=r and solving gives I(r,S) = (S/factor) * (r^(-1/w20) - 1), and by construction I(0.9,S) = S [FACT - The-Algorithm wiki]. This is the bridge from the memory state to a scheduled date: pick r, read S, get the interval. Because the curve is a power law, the interval blows up non-linearly as r -> 1, which is exactly why retention above ~0.90 costs disproportionately more reviews. The inversion is deterministic given (r, S, w20); fuzz is applied AFTER it to avoid clumping.

nodes.definition: Give the state-transition equations that move (D,S) on each review [FACT - official algorithm wiki]. Initial state after the first rating: S0(G) = w[G-1] (w0..w3 are initial stability for Again/Hard/Good/Easy); D0(G) = w4 - e^(w5*(G-1)) + 1, with D0(1)=w4. Difficulty update (linear damping + mean reversion toward D0(4), against 'ease hell'): dD = -w6*(G-3); D' = D + dD*(10-D)/9; D'' = w7*D0(4) + (1-w7)*D', clamped to [1,10]. Stability after SUCCESS (G>=2): S'_r = S*(e^{w8}*(11-D)*S^{-w9}*(e^{w10*(1-R)}-1)*w15[if G=2]*w16[if G=4] + 1), with SInc=S'/S >= 1, shrinking as D and S rise and GROWING as R drops (the spacing effect), converging to an upper bound for overdue-but-recalled cards. Stability after LAPSE (G=1): S'_f = w11*D^{-w12}*((S+1)^{w13}-1)*e^{w14*(1-R)}. Same-day (short-term): S'(S,G) = S*e^{w17*(G-3+w18)}*S^{-w19}.

nodes.definition: Establish desired retention r as the SINGLE workload knob the operator actually tunes. In the SM-2 world the rough equivalent is the interval modifier log(desired%)/log(current%): raising 85%->90% is ~35% more reviews for +5 points, consistent with the exponential blow-up near r->1. r is set per-preset, not per-card, and is the one number that trades knowledge against time.

nodes.definition: Model the workload-vs-retention relationship as U-shaped, not monotone [FACT - The-Optimal-Retention wiki + deck-options.md]. Two opposing forces: higher r -> shorter intervals -> more reviews; lower r -> more forgetting -> more relearning. Their sum has a minimum, so there is a workload-MINIMIZING retention. Anki's CMRR ('Compute minimum recommended retention') searches for it, and choosing a retention BELOW that minimum is strictly dominated — you spend more time AND retain less. Total knowledge is approximated by the sum of R across all cards, so the operator's real objective is 'maximize retained knowledge per review minute', for which r should sit at or above CMRR, never below. This is the node that turns the retention knob from a preference into an optimization.

nodes.definition: Add fuzz so a deterministic scheduler does not clump. Because I(r,S) is deterministic, cards introduced together and graded the same get identical intervals and re-surface as a spike on the same day; Anki applies random fuzz on answering 'to prevent cards that were introduced at the same time and given the same ratings from sticking together', and it CANNOT be disabled [FACT - studying.md]. Exact ranges: fuzz delta = 1 day + 0.15*(days in 2.5-7) + 0.10*(days in 7-20) + 0.05*(days > 20); short intervals are not fuzzed; learning cards get up to 5 minutes extra delay [FACT - fuzz.rs FUZZ_RANGES]. The design rule: apply fuzz AFTER the deterministic interval inversion, and any homegrown scheduler should randomize on the same banded scale.

nodes.definition: Define how fitted FSRS parameters cross the boundary. Parameters live per deck-options PRESET; Anki's protobuf DeckConfig carries repeated float fsrs_params_4/5/6 and desired_retention, with a per-deck desired_retention override [FACT - deck_config.proto lines 135-137, 188, 222]. So parameters can be read/written wherever deck config is accessible: the UI copy-paste field, or getDeckConfig/saveDeckConfig over AnkiConnect. [ESTIMATE, medium: the fetched AnkiConnect README's getDeckConfig sample predates FSRS, so whether CURRENT Anki surfaces the fsrs params through that specific call was not directly verified this session — treat it as likely-but-unconfirmed.] The clean alternative that avoids Anki entirely: feed revlog-shaped history to py-fsrs or fsrs-rs, both of which expose optimize + schedule (fsrs-rs README: 'full training support', examples schedule / optimize / migrate). The design should keep the fitted vector versioned (FSRS-4/5/6) so it lands in the matching fsrs_params field.

included: per-preset DeckConfig fsrs_params_4/5/6 + desired_retention override
the UI-field and getDeckConfig/saveDeckConfig access paths with the ESTIMATE caveat
the py-fsrs/fsrs-rs external optimize+schedule route and version-matched export

pros.claim: Because params are a per-preset versioned float field, a fitted vector can be exported via config or bypassed entirely with an external FSRS engine
pros.example: optimizing with fsrs-rs on exported revlog and writing the vector into fsrs_params_6 without Anki's optimizer

cons.claim: The exact AnkiConnect route for FSRS params is unconfirmed here and a version-mismatched vector lands in the wrong field
cons.example: writing a v5 vector into fsrs_params_6, or assuming getDeckConfig returns params it may not surface

failure_modes: writing a fitted vector into the wrong fsrs_params_N field for its version
assuming getDeckConfig surfaces FSRS params without confirming against a live client
exporting params without their FSRS version tag
acceptance_tests: the design states the per-preset DeckConfig fsrs_params_4/5/6 + desired_retention fields, the access paths with the getDeckConfig ESTIMATE caveat, and the py-fsrs/fsrs-rs external route with version-matched export
revisit_triggers: a live client confirms or refutes getDeckConfig FSRS-param surfacing
the DeckConfig proto adds a new fsrs_params field
an external engine's optimize API changes

base.update_signal: a live confirmation of getDeckConfig or a new fsrs_params field revises the export path

nodes.definition: Choose the interop path of least resistance [FACT - scheduling-implications section]. For COLD delivery, generate content as .apkg via genanki with STABLE note GUIDs so re-imports update; for LIVE round-trip, use AnkiConnect to create/update notes and read getReviewsOfCards telemetry back. Grade vocabulary stays Anki's 1-4 internally, mapping to SM-2's 0-5 only at import boundaries (Anki's FAQ explains four grades suffice because failures are rare). The revlog-shaped history from REVLOG_LOGGING is the currency that flows both ways: exportable via genanki/importPackage and writable via insertReviews. Because Anki is NOT installed in this build, the genanki cold path is the only one exercisable here; the AnkiConnect live path is designed but must be validated against a real client. Decision: default to genanki .apkg for delivery, layer AnkiConnect for users who run Anki live, and never let a non-1-4 grade or an unstable GUID cross the boundary.

included: genanki .apkg for cold delivery + AnkiConnect for live round-trip
grade held at 1-4, mapped to 0-5 only at import
revlog as the two-way currency and the genanki-only-exercisable-here caveat
excluded: the final go/no-go composition (its own node)

pros.claim: Splitting cold (genanki) from live (AnkiConnect) interop gives a path that works with or without a running Anki and keeps history flowing both ways
pros.example: shipping decks as .apkg to everyone and adding AnkiConnect telemetry only for users who run Anki

cons.claim: The live AnkiConnect half cannot be validated in this build, so the two-path design carries an unverified branch until a real client tests it
cons.example: committing to a getReviewsOfCards telemetry loop that was never exercised against a live Anki here

failure_modes: letting a non-1-4 grade or unstable GUID cross the interop boundary
relying on the AnkiConnect live path as if it were verified in this build
duplicating cards because the cold and live paths use different GUID rules
acceptance_tests: the design defaults to genanki .apkg (stable GUIDs) for cold delivery, layers AnkiConnect for live round-trip with grades held at 1-4, uses revlog as the two-way currency, and flags that only the genanki path is exercisable in this build
revisit_triggers: a real Anki client validates the AnkiConnect path
the interop grade or GUID contract changes
a duplication or history-loss is observed across the boundary

base.update_signal: a live-client validation or an interop-contract change revises the path decision

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: a scheduler design is a GO when it satisfies every binding property at once. (1) It is an explicit (grade, elapsed) -> next-state/interval function, response- AND time-dependent (not SM-2-time-blind). (2) It logs reviews in revlog shape from day one, so per-user parameter optimization stays possible. (3) It prefers FSRS/DSR for maturity but can fall back to the classic-Anki SM-2 variant, mapping grades to 1-4. (4) It applies fuzz after the deterministic interval inversion. (5) It sets desired retention at or above CMRR on the U-shaped workload curve, never below. (6) It integrates with Anki only through verified public surfaces (genanki .apkg for cold delivery; AnkiConnect designed but validated against a real client, since Anki is not installed here). Reconciled refusals: do not ship a time-blind scheduler; do not defer revlog logging; do not set retention below CMRR; do not disable fuzz; do not claim any AnkiConnect live behavior as verified in this build; do not invent an effect size or algorithm constant the research did not confirm. A design that meets the math but fails a gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

included: the six go conditions (contract, revlog-from-day-one, model choice, fuzz, retention>=CMRR, verified-surface interop)
the named refusals
the gate-must-clear rule
excluded: the per-node detail each condition rests on

pros.claim: The merged verdict prevents shipping a scheduler that is mathematically fine but violates a logging, workload or honesty gate
pros.example: withholding a go from a design that computes intervals correctly but defers revlog logging

cons.claim: A single verdict can flatten trade-offs (e.g. SM-2 simplicity vs FSRS accuracy) that a specific deployment might weigh differently
cons.example: a low-volume deployment for which the classic SM-2 variant is genuinely enough being judged against FSRS

failure_modes: issuing a go on the interval math alone while a revlog, fuzz or retention gate is unmet
claiming AnkiConnect live behavior as verified in a build where Anki is absent
treating the verdict as static when a new FSRS version or reachable source changes a gate
acceptance_tests: the verdict lists the six go conditions, states the named refusals, conditions every go on clearing its binding gate, and marks the AnkiConnect live path unverified in this build
revisit_triggers: a new FSRS version or a reachable primary source changes a gate
a deployment's volume makes SM-2-vs-FSRS trade differently
a live client changes the interop verification status

base.update_signal: a new FSRS version, a reachable source, or a live-client status change revises the verdict

the optimizer fits the parameters that appear in the stability/difficulty update equations

the .apkg/.colpkg package wraps the SQLite database whose schema is defined here
AnkiConnect's insertReviews and card actions read/write the revlog and cards columns
genanki emits exactly the .apkg package format defined here
the versioned parameter vector is the object the export path carries into DeckConfig
the fitted vector produced by optimization is what gets exported per preset

AnkiConnect is the live-round-trip half of the interop decision
parameter export is part of what crosses the interop boundary

SM-2 grows intervals geometrically without bound while FSRS's stability gain is bounded and time-aware
edges.resolution_rule: prefer the FSRS/DSR model for its bounded, time-aware stability gain; keep SM-2 only as a transparent reference oracle and an import-boundary format, not the production scheduler

edges.why_related: the mandatory elapsed-time input contradicts SM-2's assumption that reviews happen on schedule
edges.resolution_rule: treat SM-2's on-time assumption as a defect: credit actual elapsed time (Anki days_late) or, preferably, use FSRS's R(t,S) so overdue reviews are scheduled from real elapsed days

edges.why_related: shipping the fixed FSRS-6 default vector pulls against fitting a per-user vector on the user's own revlog
edges.resolution_rule: start new users on the versioned default vector as a cold-start, then replace it with the per-preset optimized vector once enough revlog exists, reoptimizing about monthly

edges.why_related: offline .apkg generation and live AnkiConnect round-trip are two competing integration paths with different guarantees
edges.resolution_rule: default to genanki .apkg for cold delivery (works with no running Anki, as in this build) and add AnkiConnect only for users who run Anki live, keeping one stable-GUID / 1-4-grade contract across both

edges.why_related: fuzz's randomness fights the pure-deterministic ideal of the (grade,elapsed) transition
edges.resolution_rule: keep the interval inversion deterministic and pure, then apply fuzz as a final, clearly separated post-step so tests assert on a band rather than an exact date

edges.why_related: running your own optimizer vs exporting to Anki's optimizer are two competing ways to own the fit
edges.resolution_rule: own the fit with py-fsrs/fsrs-rs on exported revlog when you need control, but export the version-matched vector into the correct fsrs_params_N field so Anki and the external engine agree

edges.why_related: both are (grade, elapsed) schedulers Anki ships as built-in algorithms, so they share the review-button and revlog surface
the optimizer consumes exactly the revlog schema shape, so the logged columns constrain what can be fit
the spacing effect is why targeting a retention (rather than massing reviews) improves retained knowledge per minute

conflict_axes.name: response_only_vs_response_plus_time
conflict_axes.description: SM-2 schedules on the grade alone and assumes on-time review, while classic Anki and FSRS make actual elapsed time a first-class input.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make elapsed time mandatory: prefer FSRS's native R(t,S), or at minimum Anki's days_late credit, never a purely time-blind SM-2 in production

conflict_axes.name: unbounded_geometric_vs_bounded_stability_gain
conflict_axes.description: SM-2/Anki grow the interval as a geometric EF*interval jump while FSRS's SInc is bounded and shrinks as stability rises.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer the bounded FSRS stability gain for mature cards; use SM-2's geometric growth only as a reference, not the shipped model

conflict_axes.name: higher_retention_vs_lower_workload
conflict_axes.description: Raising desired retention shortens intervals and adds reviews, while lowering it adds relearning, so the two goals pull apart.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set desired retention at or above CMRR on the U-shaped curve, never below, and treat above ~0.97 as overwhelming

conflict_axes.name: deterministic_schedule_vs_fuzz
conflict_axes.description: A pure deterministic interval is reproducible but clumps sibling cards, while fuzz de-clumps at the cost of reproducibility.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the inversion deterministic and apply mandatory fuzz as a separated post-step; assert tests on a band, not an exact date

conflict_axes.name: six_grade_resolution_vs_four_button_simplicity
conflict_axes.description: SM-2's 0-5 scale carries more failure resolution while Anki/FSRS's four buttons are simpler and argue failures are rare.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: normalize internally to 1-4 for revlog/optimizer/import consistency and map 0-5 only at import boundaries

conflict_axes.name: default_params_vs_per_user_optimization
conflict_axes.description: Shipping the fixed FSRS-6 defaults is simplest but a per-user fit on revlog tracks the individual's forgetting far better.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cold-start on the versioned defaults, then reoptimize per preset once enough revlog accrues (about monthly)

conflict_axes.name: cold_apkg_delivery_vs_live_ankiconnect
conflict_axes.description: Offline genanki .apkg works without Anki but is one-way, while AnkiConnect gives live round-trip but needs a running client absent in this build.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to genanki cold delivery and layer AnkiConnect only for live users, validating the live path against a real client before relying on it

conflict_axes.name: verified_source_vs_unreachable_canonical
conflict_axes.description: The canonical SM-2 page, the psychology journals and the rendered Anki docs were egress-blocked, so claims rest on source repos/mirrors rather than the primary pages.
poles: cite only the fetched source repo / mirror and tag the rest UNKNOWN
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the source honesty in the prose: FACT for fetched source-repo/mirror content, UNKNOWN with a named blocker for unreachable primary figures, never an invented number

conflict_axes.name: own_optimizer_vs_reuse_fsrs_engine
conflict_axes.description: Building a bespoke optimizer competes with reusing py-fsrs/fsrs-rs, which already expose optimize + schedule on revlog.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reuse the maintained FSRS engines on revlog-shaped history unless a specific need forces a bespoke build, and keep the vector version-matched

conflict_axes.name: lapse_reset_vs_stability_preservation
conflict_axes.description: Anki's New Interval can fully reset a lapsed card while FSRS preserves a difficulty-scaled residual stability, trading forgetting-safety against wasted reviews.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use FSRS's lapse-stability form (or a non-zero New Interval) so a single miss does not discard all accumulated stability, while still relearning

edge_cases.description: A scheduler is shipped that ignores actual elapsed time (SM-2-style) and mis-schedules overdue cards
edge_cases.trigger: the design keys the next interval on grade and repetition count only, not elapsed days
edge_cases.mitigation: make elapsed_days a mandatory transition input and use FSRS R(t,S) or Anki days_late credit so overdue reviews schedule from real elapsed time

edge_cases.description: Review logging is deferred, so per-user parameter optimization is impossible later
edge_cases.trigger: the scheduler launches on default params without persisting revlog rows from the first review
edge_cases.mitigation: log the full revlog record (timestamp_ms, item_id, grade 1-4, interval, last_interval, duration_ms, type) from day one even on default params

edge_cases.description: A 0-5 SM-2 grade leaks into a log or scheduler expecting 1-4, corrupting intervals and fits
edge_cases.trigger: an import boundary passes SM-2 quality grades through without mapping to 1-4
edge_cases.mitigation: normalize internally to 1-4 and convert SM-2 0-5 only at the import boundary with an explicit mapping

edge_cases.description: Desired retention is set below CMRR to 'study less', costing more time AND less knowledge
edge_cases.trigger: an operator lowers r past the workload-minimizing point assuming lower retention always means less work
edge_cases.mitigation: compute CMRR and refuse retentions below it; explain that below the minimum the relearning tail dominates

edge_cases.description: The scheduler ships without fuzz and cards introduced together return as daily review spikes
edge_cases.trigger: the deterministic interval inversion is used as the final due date with no randomization
edge_cases.mitigation: apply Anki-style banded fuzz (1 day + 15%/10%/5% bands, 5-min learning delay) after inversion

edge_cases.description: An .apkg is exported with 'Include Scheduling Information' off and all review history is stripped on import
edge_cases.trigger: a deck package is created without scheduling info and used to move a schedule
edge_cases.mitigation: export .apkg with scheduling info on when the schedule must travel, and reserve .colpkg for whole-collection moves

edge_cases.description: An AnkiConnect integration is assumed to work in a build environment where Anki is not installed
edge_cases.trigger: an integration test targets 127.0.0.1:8765 with no running Anki client
edge_cases.mitigation: treat AnkiConnect live behavior as UNKNOWN in this build, exercise only the genanki offline path here, and validate the live path against a real client

edge_cases.description: genanki re-import duplicates cards because Note.guid was hashed from all fields
edge_cases.trigger: a card is edited and re-exported with a GUID derived from every field value
edge_cases.mitigation: derive Note.guid from a stable key field and hardcode model_id/deck_id so re-imports update instead of duplicate

edge_cases.description: A fitted FSRS parameter vector from one version is written into the wrong fsrs_params_N field
edge_cases.trigger: a v5 vector is exported into an FSRS-6 preset (or vice versa) without a version tag
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every vector tagged with its FSRS version and write it only into the matching fsrs_params_4/5/6 field

edge_cases.description: Anki's cards.factor is written as a raw float ease instead of permille and misread when FSRS is on
edge_cases.trigger: a 2.5 ease is stored as 2.5 rather than 2500, or revlog.factor is read as ease while FSRS reuses it for difficulty
edge_cases.mitigation: store ease as permille (2500=2.5x) and branch on whether FSRS is enabled before interpreting factor as ease vs difficulty

edge_cases.description: An Ebbinghaus/Cepeda/Roediger effect size is quoted as fact although the primary source was unreachable
edge_cases.trigger: a citation's exact figures are asserted from memory rather than a fetched source
edge_cases.mitigation: state the bibliographic reference as FACT, the one-line finding as ESTIMATE, and hold exact figures UNKNOWN until the primary source is fetched

edge_cases.description: The optimizer is run on sparse or imported revlog and produces an unstable parameter vector
edge_cases.trigger: reoptimization is triggered too early or over stale imported logs without an ignore-before date
edge_cases.mitigation: wait for enough revlog, reoptimize about monthly, and set 'Ignore cards reviewed before' to exclude stale imported history

dominance_rules.rule: Elapsed time dominates a purely response-based interval
dominance_rules.rationale: ignoring actual elapsed time (SM-2's blind spot) mis-schedules overdue and mature cards
dominance_rules.trigger: a scheduler computes the next interval from grade and repetition count alone
dominance_rules.action: make elapsed_days a mandatory input and use FSRS R(t,S) or Anki days_late credit

dominance_rules.rule: Revlog-from-day-one dominates any later logging convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: per-user optimization is impossible retroactively without the review history
dominance_rules.trigger: a launch plan defers review logging or logs a non-revlog shape
dominance_rules.action: persist the full revlog record from the first review, even on default parameters

dominance_rules.rule: The internal 1-4 grade vocabulary dominates any source scale
dominance_rules.rationale: revlog, optimizer and Anki import all speak 1-4, so a mixed scale corrupts intervals and fits
dominance_rules.trigger: a 0-5 or other grade scale enters the log or scheduler
dominance_rules.action: normalize to 1-4 internally and map foreign scales only at import boundaries

dominance_rules.rule: CMRR dominates a 'study less' retention cut
dominance_rules.rationale: below the workload-minimizing retention the relearning tail costs more time and less knowledge
dominance_rules.trigger: an operator sets desired retention below CMRR to reduce reviews
dominance_rules.action: compute CMRR and refuse retentions below it, explaining the dominated region

dominance_rules.rule: Mandatory fuzz dominates the deterministic-reproducibility ideal
dominance_rules.rationale: deterministic intervals clump sibling cards into review spikes and Anki does not allow disabling fuzz
dominance_rules.trigger: the deterministic inversion is used directly as the due date
dominance_rules.action: apply banded fuzz after inversion and assert tests on a band, not an exact date

dominance_rules.rule: Verified public surfaces dominate assumed live behavior
dominance_rules.rationale: Anki is not installed in this build, so AnkiConnect live calls cannot be confirmed here
dominance_rules.trigger: an integration relies on AnkiConnect behavior in this environment
dominance_rules.action: exercise only the genanki offline path here and mark live AnkiConnect behavior UNKNOWN until a real client validates it

dominance_rules.rule: The FSRS version tag dominates a bare parameter vector
dominance_rules.rationale: a v4/5/6 vector is only valid for its engine and field, so an untagged vector mis-schedules silently
dominance_rules.trigger: a parameter vector is exported or stored without its FSRS version
dominance_rules.action: tag every vector with its FSRS version and write it only into the matching fsrs_params_N field

dominance_rules.rule: Fetched-source honesty dominates a convenient citation
dominance_rules.rationale: canonical pages and journals were egress-blocked, so only source-repo/mirror content is FACT
dominance_rules.trigger: an algorithm constant or effect size is asserted from an unreachable primary source
dominance_rules.action: tag it FACT only if fetched, else ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN with the named blocker, and never invent a number

dominance_rules.rule: Bounded FSRS stability gain dominates SM-2 geometric growth for mature cards
dominance_rules.rationale: unbounded EF*interval growth over-extends mature-card intervals that FSRS bounds and time-adjusts
dominance_rules.trigger: interval growth for a mature card is computed geometrically
dominance_rules.action: use the FSRS success-stability form so the gain converges rather than compounding without bound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design the (grade, elapsed) transition and revlog shape before choosing a specific algorithm
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking the whole logging and interface layer when swapping SM-2 for FSRS later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log the full revlog record from the first review, even on default parameters
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering per-user optimization is impossible because the history was never captured

anti_rework_rules.rule: Normalize grades to 1-4 internally and map foreign scales only at import boundaries
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mixed 0-5/1-4 log that corrupts every interval and optimizer fit and must be re-derived

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute CMRR before setting desired retention
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a below-CMRR retention that has to be walked back after workload rises and knowledge falls

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply fuzz as a separated post-step and assert tests on a band from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: brittle exact-date tests that break the moment mandatory fuzz is added

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every FSRS parameter vector with its version and target fsrs_params_N field at export time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a version-mismatched vector silently mis-scheduling until it is traced and re-exported

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat AnkiConnect as unverified in this build and exercise only the genanki path here
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an integration built against assumed live behavior that fails when first run on a real client

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags on every algorithmic claim as it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented constant or effect size having to be retracted from the design after review

priority_rationale: The scheduler contract, grade vocabulary and elapsed-time input come first because every algorithm and every log depends on the (grade, elapsed) signature and a single grade scale; the SM-2 baseline, classic-Anki variant and FSRS DSR model, forgetting curve, interval inversion and state-update equations next, because they are the memory-model math that turns the contract into intervals; the desired-retention knob and the U-shaped workload curve then make workload an explicit optimization; revlog logging, the schema map and per-user optimization come next because logging from day one is what makes optimization possible at all; the fuzz, file-format, AnkiConnect, genanki and FSRS-param-export nodes then build the integration surface on the schema; and the interop decision and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a delivery path and a defensible verified-surface verdict, with the empirical basis grounding the honesty gate throughout.
